objectives.summary: The project focuses on developing an mRNA LPNP immune regulatory factor for tumor immunotherapy, aiming to address the limitations of existing immune checkpoint inhibitors. Key milestones include project initiation in Q1 2023, execution from Q2 to Q4 2023, and finalization by Q3 2024, with an IND application planned for early 2026.
key_points: The project aims to develop IL-10@NPs for tumor immunotherapy to improve upon existing immune checkpoint inhibitors.

The project includes the design and development of a cationic lipid library and preclinical evaluations.
The organization plans to apply for at least 8 invention patents within the first four milestones.
The project aims to submit an IND application for IL-10@NPs in early 2026.

innovation.summary: The project introduces innovative mRNA delivery technologies, including a universal linear mRNA scaffold and unique cap modifications that enhance protein expression and address delivery system challenges. The development of a circular mRNA platform and adhesive mRNA drug delivery system further distinguishes this project, supported by preclinical evidence demonstrating efficacy in tumor treatment.
key_points: The universal linear mRNA scaffold is designed to express any protein and addresses challenges in expressing long fragments.
Innovative cap modifications enhance translation efficiency and overcome existing patent restrictions.
The project has developed a circular mRNA platform that utilizes an intron self-splicing principle.
Preclinical results show that IL-10 mRNA@NPs significantly enhance tumor-infiltrating CD8+ T cell proliferation and exhibit anti-tumor effects.
The adhesive mRNA drug delivery platform enables localized delivery to mucosal organs, improving treatment efficacy.
The project leader's team has pioneered a scalable mRNA synthesis and delivery technology with independent intellectual property rights.
risks: The project faces challenges related to existing patent restrictions on lipid structures and formulations.
The technology must effectively address key challenges faced by delivery systems to be successful.
mitigations: The unique scaffold and cap modification are designed to overcome international cap modification patents.
The universal linear mRNA scaffold is suitable for any protein expression and addresses the challenges of expressing long fragments.

The project benefits from a simplified mRNA preparation process and a long half-life, which reduces costs and dosing frequency. However, there are risks associated with the targeting of tumor tissues, which need to be addressed.
